shortDefinition: The practice of having human assessors judge AI output quality, usefulness, or correctness as a complement or alternative to automated metrics.
fullDefinition: Human evaluation is the gold standard for assessing AI systems when automated metrics are insufficient. Human evaluators — often domain experts or representative users — judge outputs based on criteria like accuracy, helpfulness, coherence, safety, and alignment with instructions. Human evaluation is essential because automated metrics like benchmark scores can miss important qualities like tone, nuance, creativity, and user satisfaction. Common methods include side-by-side comparisons where evaluators choose the better of two model outputs, Likert scales for rating quality, and red-teaming exercises to probe safety failures. Despite being slower and more expensive than automated evaluation, human judgment remains irreplaceable for understanding real-world AI performance.
examples: Evaluators rating chatbot responses on a 1-5 helpfulness scale
Comparing two model outputs side-by-side to determine which is better
Red teamers attempting to find safety failures in an AI assistant
